newsitem.title: ISRAEL: NETANYAHU HOPES TO END GOVERNMENT LAND MONOPOLY.
newsitem.headline: NETANYAHU HOPES TO END GOVERNMENT LAND MONOPOLY.

text.p: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said on Thursday the government hoped to end the state's near-monopoly on the ownership of land.
"We also want to make radical changes here in the huge monopoly," Netanyahu said in wide-ranging remarks to members of his Likud party that were broadcast on Israeli radio stations.

"(Infrastructure) Minister (Ariel) Sharon will bring a proposal to the government that I intend to support enabling the sale of apartments or more accurately the transfer of ownership of apartments...to achieve more flexibility in the land market."
The state owns most of the land in the country, which is administered and tendered under 99-year leases by the Israel Lands Administration.
Netanyahu also said he planned to authorise new television channels, recommend allowing satellite broadcasts and propose other changes in the broadcast media. He did not elaborate.
Israel has two television stations -- one state-run and the other privately controlled -- as well as cable television.
